text: Every other R B M K was changed. The control rods were redesigned, and a faster emergency shutdown system was added. The fuel was made slightly richer, and extra absorbers were added, to tame that feedback loop. And the minimum number of rods that must stay in the core was raised sharply. An international safety review later concluded that the reactor's design flaws were central to the disaster, not just the operators' mistakes. Today, reactor four sits under a giant steel arch, slid into place in twenty sixteen. A safety button that can make things worse isn't really a safety button. What other machine do you know with a button that could backfire? Tell me in the comments.
